messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps based on what we discussed: 

Summary of perf targets you mentioned:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target 200-250 ms for product-page interactions (goal: <=250 ms).
- Streaming: you prefer WebSocket for the product UI; SSE is acceptable for some backend jobs.
- Chunk cadence: ideally chunks every ~150-250 ms to keep progressive render smooth.
- Throughput & concurrency: target sustained 150 RPS across peak traffic windows, concurrent active sessions ~50.
- Regional requirement: US-first, with a potential EU rollout later.

Ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the TTFT vs throughput tradeoff priority (i.e., is TTFT > throughput or vice versa)?
2) Please share any network constraints (e.g., CloudFront / Cloudflare in front of calls) and whether you have edge TTLs that could affect streaming.
3) I attached a preliminary SLO matrix (slo_matrix.xlsx) — can you review and flag anything off?
4) If these look right, propose a 45-min technical deep-dive with your infra/engineer + our SE to scope a short POC (measurement plan + success criteria).

Proposed slots (PST): Mon 8/23 10:00-10:45, Tue 8/24 11:00-11:45, Wed 8/25 09:00-09:45.

I'll loop in Marissa to help scope the POC and confirm implementation considerations for streaming cadence.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO candidate table)

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acmeretail.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the key points from our side: 

- TTFT: yes, product team wants TTFT in the 200-250 ms window. If you can get below 200 ms in the POC that would be great but not required for launch.
- Streaming: WebSocket preferred for the in-app experience. SSE could be a fallback for dashboards.
- Chunk cadence: target ~150 ms cadence for the initial progressive render, then larger chunks for subsequent content — anything up to 250 ms is acceptable.
- Throughput/concurrency: expect ~120-180 RPS during peak depending on promotions; plan for 50 concurrent interactive sessions.

A couple of constraints to call out: we front traffic with CloudFront and sometimes terminate TLS on the edge, which can add 20-70 ms depending on region. I'm attaching a small sample network trace we ran earlier (network_trace_sample.txt) that shows a cold-cache edge hop.

Next steps: the product and infra teams want a POC that measures TTFT at the client (browser) level and server-to-client chunk cadence. We'll need a runbook for measurement and a config for both WebSocket and SSE endpoints.

I'm available Tue 8/24 11:00-12:00 PST for the technical call. If that works, let's lock it.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
VP Product, Acme Retail
sarah@acmeretail.com

Thanks Sarah — Tue 8/24 11:00 PST works great. I've locked that slot tentatively. For the technical deep-dive, here's the proposed agenda and measurement plan so we come prepared: 

Agenda (45 min):
- 5m introductions & objective alignment
- 10m measurement strategy (where we measure TTFT: client-side vs edge vs server)
- 15m streaming feasibility (WebSocket vs SSE, chunk cadence control, backpressure, ACKs)
- 10m POC scope & timeline (test harness, traffic profile, success criteria)
- 5m next steps & owners

Measurement plan (high level):
- TTFT: measure from browser (first byte of streaming chunk that produces visible token) and compare to server-side measured generation first-token time. Include edge/ingress latency delta.
- Chunk cadence: instrument client to capture arrival timestamps for each chunk (ms resolution). Goal: median cadence <=200 ms, 95th <=350 ms during steady state.
- Throughput: run 10-20 minute sustained run at 150 RPS to observe P99 TTFT and chunk cadence degradation.

Pre-POC asks:
- Can you share any WAF / CDN config that might terminate long-lived sockets?
- Will you allow a test origin that bypasses some edge caching for baseline measurements?

I'll attach the network trace you sent to the POC ticket. Marissa — can you confirm any server-side pre-checks we should ask the customer's infra team to run (e.g., max concurrent sockets, keepalive timeouts, proxy timeouts)? Lauren — could you prep a short checklist for the POC infra (Docker image, example client harness, scripts to measure chunk cadence)?

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
